reviews.text: qué recuerdos cuando ganó por mejores vfx... twitter was on fire y salieron los takes más malos ever diciendo "CÓMO VA A GANAR 1917 SI APENAS TIENE EFECTOS ESPECIALES???!!!" y film twt usando el vfx breakdown de esta aniquilando por completo those claims ufff me daba la risa pero fue frustrante ver a tanta gente biased ahora mismo estoy viéndome pelis bélicas, especialmente si tienen algo de subtext queer preparándome para la bola negra . aquí hay un poco la homoerótica inherente en este género muy muy sutil, pero conecto tan poco con la peli... i will quote a allan arkush que dijo: " All I remembered was the shots not human moments " y es lo que me pasa con esta (y lo mismo que me pasa con dune ) que es todo muy espectacular pero me deja sin más. tiene una iluminación preciosa gracias a deakins, el acting, el sound design y los sets una maravilla, rip las piernas del cámara... pero al final el oner distrae demasiado just for them to do stitches anyways. ofc tiene secuencias increíbles e icónicas como la de él corriendo y chocando con soldados pero con el resto de la peli se siente más flashy que otra cosa. como dijo schrader: "la pregunta ya no es cómo lo han hecho sino por qué" la aprecio bastante por todo el trabajo que hay detrás pero es casi lo único en lo que pienso cuando la veo.

Superbe reproduction historique. Un film à gros budget sensationnel. Avec une superbe technique et un défis de "plan séquence" très réussi qui donne une approche intéressante à l'œuvre avec une tension et une sensation de suivi en temps réel. Quelques références qui font plaisirs et des acteurs de qualités. Cependant, rien de révolutionnaire, un scénario basique, une approche cinématographique de film grand publique. C'est donc un bon film.

I feel like i'm probably going to get attacked for only giving this 3 stars because this movie is INSANELY WELL MADE, but i just didn't connect with it as much as i thought i would. The biggest thing about 1917 is obviously the one-shot style, and yeah, it's fucking impressive. The way the camera follows Schofield and Blake through the trenches, fields and destroyed villages makes you feel like you're actually waling through WW1 with them. There were definitely moments where i completely forgot about the camera and just got sucked into what was happening. And visually, this movie is ridiculous. Roger Deakins absolutely cooked. The lighting, the landscapes, the trenches, the burning buildings at night - there are so many shots where i was just thinking  "how did they even film this?" The opening section with Schofield and Blake was probably my favourite. Their friendship feels natural, and i actually cared about what happened to them. George MacKay is also really good, especially as the movie gets more intense and Schofield is basically running on fear and adrenaline. But i think that's where my problem is. I admired the filmmaking way more than i connected with the actual story. The "one continuous shot" idea is amazing technically, but sometimes it felt like the gimmick was more interesting to me than the characters. There are also quite a few moments where i could almost see the movie setting up the next impressive shot or sequence. The film is definitely at it's best when it slows down and lets you actually sit with what's happening. The scenes where Schofield is just walking through the aftermath of everything are honestly more affecting to me than some of the bigger action sequences. It makes war feel less like an epic story and more like a horrible, exhausting place that these young men have been thrown into. The final stretch was probably the closest i got to being completely invested. Watching Schofield desperately trying to to reach the soldiers while everything is falling apart around him had me properly stressed. Incredible cinematography, great performances, amazing atmosphere, but i was more impressed than emotionally destroyed. 3/5

Apesar de render bons momentos, a filmagem desse filme é estressante, ela omite uma parte gigantesca do filme gravando apenas uma coisa afastando o espectador do espaço em que o filme sem encontra, trazendo apenas narrativa como aspecto para contar o filme e uma imagem porca que não busca gravar nada. Momentos de dramatização são ruins de enxergar, momentos de ação são ocultados e mostram apenas poeira subindo e o protagonista se preparando para dar continuidade ao plano sequência. Além disso, a freneticidade do filme sempre ignora os sentimentos de cenas anteriores com objetivo de justapor por novas e sempre criando essas novas de forma muita rápida, fazendo com que cenas como a morte do amigo do protagonista tenham seus sentimentos esvaidos rapidamente, quase como na lógica de uma série onde o próximo momento sempre será mais importante que o atual.

El dolor, la pérdida ,la muerte y el trauma son las temáticas que siempre se han usado historicamente en el cine bélico desde que como civilización hemos decidió matarnos unos a otros.Esta película, muy al margen de ser espléndidamente dirigida y con ese plano secuencia infinito que te sumerge en la historia, muestra esas cuatro fases que se ha vivido debido al trauma social de la guerra. A pesar de un tanto idealizar al personaje principal y tratar a la guerra como un medio para el desarrollo de objetivos de un hombre, también muestra que a pesar de tanto horror seguimos sobreviviendo y nos resistimos a morir por intitno por el amor y por resistencia a irse fácilmente.

Sam Mendes — THE FORMALIST!! Sam Mendes continues to walk in Christopher Nolan's shadow when it comes to his big-budget films. It was clear in Skyfall and clear in Spectre . These are films that want to be more than just action and adventure. It might sound harsh, but he wears his influences openly. He wants to make big films that are also important films! Much has been said about the choice to make the film appear as if shot in a single take, and yes, it largely works — because every department is striving for perfection. Otherwise, it's easy for long takes to become an exercise in "good enough," so as to avoid having to redo them. But here, the tension is maintained more or less throughout. It's difficult to speculate how the film would have played conventionally edited, because it would have needed an entirely different story — as it now hinges entirely on unfolding in real time, with no room for deeper dives into either characters or themes. So it's fairly pointless to entertain that thought experiment. The main thing is that the stylistic choice has been made, it's followed through, and it makes the film feel more significant than it might otherwise have been. The story doesn’t come with any sort of surprises whatsoever. It is only novel in the way it is told. Form and story in symbiosis. The problem I have is that it becomes so controlled — the sense of danger rarely comes through as clearly as it could. When it works, it works, but it comes a little too rarely, since we are constantly being pushed forward and forward.
